newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gunman holed up in Swiss church after shooting two.
newsitem.headline: Gunman holed up in Swiss church after shooting two.

text.p: Armed police on Saturday night surrounded a church in the heart of Geneva where a gunman was holed up after shooting and wounding two worshippers, police said.
Police said the unidentified gunman, aged 52, from a German-speaking part of Switzerland wounded the two people with a pistol after entering Notre Dame Roman Catholic church at around 1830 GMT.
Reuter photographer Pascal Volery, who was the the scene, said the man was now alone in the church which is near Geneva's main train station and the four-star Hotel Cornavin.
A policeman and a psychologist were in contact with him trying to persuade him to come out.
Earlier police spokesman Alexander Baerisswyl said: "He's still inside. We are trying to talk to him. We sent psychologists but there has been no dialogue so far."
"If dialogue does not work we'll have to use force. The person entered the church and wounded two of the worshippers," he said.
It was not clear how badly hurt the two wounded were. Police offered no idea of what the gunman's motivation was.
Armed police crouched along the walls of the church with guns trained on the building. Police cordoned off nearby streets.
